chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mismaʿī, from Ismāʿīl ibn Yasār al-Wāsiṭī, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Do not enter the grave while you are wearing a turban, nor a cap, nor a cloak, nor shoes; and loosen your buttons."
He said: I said, "What about the khuff?" He said: "There is no harm in the khuff at the time of necessity and taqiyyah, and he should exert his utmost effort regarding that."

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary practice allowing exception in specific circumstances
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: a state of necessity that permits exception
key_terms.الْخُفِّ: leather foot-covering permitted here in necessity and taqiyyah
key_terms.الْعِمَامَةُ: a turban that should not be worn when entering the grave
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave into which one descends during burial
key_terms.حِذَاءٌ: shoes or footwear not to be worn when entering the grave
key_terms.رِدَاءٌ: an outer cloak or wrap to be removed in this context
key_terms.قَلَنْسُوَةٌ: a cap or head-covering prohibited here when descending into the grave

ai.seo_question: What should a person avoid wearing when entering the grave for burial according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the etiquette of entering the grave during burial, instructing that certain garments and footwear should not be worn. It also provides an exception for wearing khuff in cases of necessity and taqiyyah, while emphasizing striving to comply as much as possible.
